name: TypeWords
description: Practice English, one strike, one step forward; 练习英语，一次敲击，一点进步；
one_liner: A typing-practice app that teaches English vocabulary by having you type each word letter by letter, with a big library of word lists (exams, TV subtitles, books) to practice from.
buyer: A Chinese student or working professional preparing for an English exam (like the college entrance exam or CET) who wants free, low-friction daily vocabulary drilling.
business_use_cases: A language-learning content creator embeds it as a free lead magnet linking to their paid tutoring service.
A cram school in China deploys a branded, self-hosted version for students to drill assigned word lists.
An ESL app developer forks its word-list format as a starting dataset for a niche vocabulary product.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a premium tier with progress tracking, spaced repetition, and custom word-list uploads for schools.

steal_this: Fork it, add one killer word list (e.g. IELTS academic vocabulary) with spaced repetition, and sell it as a $5 one-time app to a niche exam-prep community this weekend.
